first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, while two inherited findings indicate that simplifying signup and onboarding durably improves completion, time-to-value, and activation. This is better aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than matching competitor pricing, which previously harmed 30-day retention. Verify the two most directly relevant onboarding records before committing.

final.rationale: Run a segmented onboarding-simplification experiment for SMB/simple-workspace accounts only, explicitly excluding complex-workspace accounts. The verified evidence directly addresses both current declines: signup simplification lifted activation 9% and qualified revenue 4% in SMB, while shortened onboarding improved completion 13% and time-to-value by 2.1 days for simple accounts. Guardrails should include 30- and 60-day retention, churn, and qualified revenue because signup simplification showed a small retention decline and shortened onboarding increased churn in complex workspaces. Do not pursue promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because inherited evidence indicates material retention harm.
